phase_note: Generated 2026-09-10 by the Phase 6 spec batch (wave 1) in auto-approve mode. 10 requirements / 90 acceptance criteria; 11 design components; 5 major tasks / 18 executable tasks. Step 3.5 task-graph sanity review ran as an independent reviewer subagent on Opus, read-only: round 1 NEEDS_FIXES (3 blocking, 5 should-fix, 6 notes -- all 14 applied, including splitting the oversized pass task into discovery and archive-resolution halves, correcting the merge overlay to a two-half rule so an unknown key inside a provenance record survives a refresh, and adding a governed record for the rounding offset); round 2 NEEDS_FIXES (1 blocking, 2 should-fix, 3 notes -- all applied: the forward _Depends: edge from 4.5 to 5.1 removed by giving 4.5 its own test module, requirement 5.6 moved onto the task that proves it, and four stale identifiers/wordings in design.md corrected). Per the skill's bound of one repair-and-re-review cycle, round 2's fixes were applied without a third review round; every round-2 finding was a renumber, one _Requirements: line, or a stale name, and none was a design gap (the reviewer said so explicitly). Lands the roadmap Phase 6 Existing Spec Update for athlete-benchmarks via task 5.3. Deferred, for the queue: (1) the Allen & Coggan 2nd-ed. chapter/page locator for the 0.95 x 20-minute rule is unverified, so that method ships blocked and declines by name -- the roadmap's own Direct Implementation Candidate; (2) Riegel (1981) is JSTOR-only and unread, so its citation ships as a tracked SECONDARY_ATTESTATION exception; (3) the archive-resolution rule is now stated in two passes, mitigated by an equivalence test rather than a shared private import. Cross-spec review (Phase 6 batch, 2026-09-10) round 1: I4-I6, I8, M3, M4, M6 applied; boundary lines added to 2.2, 2.3, 5.2. Round 2: R2 (2.2/2.3 boundaries -> ProfileDerivedWrite) and N2 applied.

amendments.requirement: No requirement, component, or task added, removed or renumbered; design.md and tasks.md corrected in place (Amendment 1)
amendments.reason: Queue item 2026-09-10-performance-benchmarks-design-predates-applies-from: this spec was generated by the Phase 6 batch (wave 1) against the three-field benchmark entry on main, while wave 0 (training-load Amendment 4, queue item 2026-08-27-prompt-date-strands-historical-documents) was adding a fourth recognised field, applies_from, in its worktree. The batch controller did not re-read the shared agent log between its wave 1 claim and the wave 2 dispatch, so the peer's TOUCHING line -- 'add your source field as a FIFTH entry field on top of this shape, do not re-add or reorder' -- was not seen. Wave 0 merged at 664960a; this amendment is written against that code rather than against the log line.
amendments.also: Corrections: Benchmark is kind, discipline, value, measured_on, note, applies_from and source is appended fifth after applies_from; benchmarks_to_document emits value, measured_on, applies_from, note and then source last (the file order is not the dataclass order) with the group sort key still measured_on alone; with_benchmark's source= keyword follows applies_from=; the merge's inherit-on-absent rule covers applies_from as well as note, while source's absent-then-removed rule stays deliberately asymmetric to both; the deriver never writes applies_from, so a derived entry is tier-1 only in the two-tier BenchmarkSet.applicable, and is_recorded plus the never-overwrite rule read source alone and are unaffected by dating; the merge stays scope-agnostic and every new overlay branch gains an athlete-wide fixture, because no existing fixture varies scope through the merge; task 5.3 now lands as athlete-benchmarks Amendment 2 and must read that spec's post-Amendment-1 text rather than the line numbers this plan was drafted against. A new revalidation trigger covers source's position. Phase and approvals are unchanged -- this is corrective, and the batch's own precedent is to record such an amendment in spec.json and the design rather than regenerate. Review gate (independent reviewer subagent, read-only, verified every shape claim against the landed code rather than against this amendment's prose): round 1 NEEDS_FIXES -- 1 blocking, 2 should-fix, 5 notes; all applied, no second round needed because none was a design gap. The blocking finding is the one substantive ruling in this amendment and is NOT a correction: the design asserted that is_recorded and the never-overwrite rule are unaffected by applies_from, which is true of both but left a now-false invariant standing ('a derived entry can never shadow a recorded one'). Amendment 1 created a real case -- a derived entry measured INSIDE an athlete's declared applies_from window has no same-date collision, so the pass writes it, and it then wins tier 1 for activities in the overlap, displacing the declaration. RULED ACCEPTED, not a 6.1/6.2 violation: athlete-benchmarks Req 3.10 makes tier 1 beat tier 2 unconditionally and a measurement dated nearer the activity is the better anchor whoever wrote it; Requirement 6's 'shadow' is date-scoped throughout, as this design's own Goal already said. The pass does not decline on window overlap and no DeclineReason covers it; declining would be a behavioural change needing its own criterion. The invariant, the traceability line for 6.1/6.2 and the Amendment 1 summary are all qualified to 'on its own date'. Also applied: the merge's line citation was stale BECAUSE of wave 0 (profile.py:517-583 -> 536-606, verified against main); task 2.3's survival enumeration gained the applies-from date and a fixture requirement, since 2.3 deletes and rebuilds whole groups and was the one entry-shape task the first pass did not amend; the revalidation trigger now names the four tests that actually pin the shape instead of a golden athlete.toml that does not exist. One pre-existing stale citation the reviewer found (load/engine.py:613-641, correct on main and before wave 0, so out of this amendment's scope) went to the queue.
